full_judgment:
Mr. Hasan Foez Siddique J.: These criminal petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 21.11.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case nos. 2103, 2104, 2105, 2094, 2095, 2196, 2198, 2099, 2100, 2101, 2097, 2106, 2107, 2108 and 2102 of 2012 discharging the Rules. 

 2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of these petitions, in short, are that one Mohammad Ali, on behalf of the complainant, a financial institution, field petitions of complainant which were registered as C.R. Case No.4004 of 2009, 4000 of 2009, 3999 of 2009, 4007 of 2009, 4005 of 2009 and 2028 of 2009 against the petitioner alleging, inter alia, that the petitioner being Managing Director of Crystal Bangladesh Support (Pvt.) received total amount of taka 3,75,00,000/- as loan from the complainant repayable by 60 equal monthly installments. To ensure payment against the said loan, the accused petitioner issued 60 postdated cheques in favour of complainant financial institution. The complainant produced those cheques for encashment which were bounced for insufficiency of fund. Thus, the complainant issued legal notices asking the petitioner to make payment of the amounts of the bounced cheques under the provision of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. But the petitioner did not repay the amounts mentioned in the cheques within 30 days from the date of received of those notices. Thus, the complainant filed the aforesaid cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. 

 3. The Cases were ultimately transferred in the Court of Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for holding trail. The petitioner, challenging the aforesaid proceedings, field above mentioned Criminal Miscellaneous Cases in the High Court Division under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained Rules. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order ultimately discharged all the Rules. Thus, the petitioner has filed these petitions for leave to appeal. 

 5. It is not disputed that the petitioner issued cheques. The objects of issuance of those cheques were to pay the loan amount. Definitely, the petitioner issued those cheques in favour of the complainant to recover the outstanding by producing those cheques in the Bank for encashment. Accordingly in order to realize the loan, the complainant produced the cheques in the Bank for encashment which were bounced by the Bank. In such situation, the complainant issued legal notice giving the petitioner an opportunity to pay the defaulted amount but the petitioner failed to pay the same within the stipulated period. Thus, as per provisions of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, prima-facie case against the petitioner had been made out. The High Court Division held that since there is no bar to get the loan amount realized by producing issued cheques for encashment, the instant proceeding were not liable to be quashed.
